concerns.text: FR-009 mandates a manual annotation pilot with human raters. The tasks (T017a-Code, T017b-Ingest) describe generating a payload and ingesting a manually uploaded file, but contain NO task to actually recruit raters, distribute the survey, or collect the data. T017f only logs failure. This creates a silent relaxation of FR-009: the pipeline cannot execute the mandatory human validation without an external, untracked manual step that is not part of the deliverable scope. The task list must include a mechanism (e. g., a script to generate a Prolific survey link or a documented manual protocol task) to satisfy the 'conduct' requirement of FR-009.

SC-004 requires the stability of ASR to be measured against a tolerance of ≤ 5% variance. T033a and T033b generate the sensitivity data but do NOT enforce the constraint or abort the pipeline if variance > 5%. T060 (Phase 7) adds a check, but it is a post-hoc verification task, not part of the primary execution flow. This silently relaxes the success criterion: the pipeline can complete and produce results that violate SC-004 without triggering a failure state in the main run. The constraint enforcement must be moved to Phase 5 (T033b or a new T033c) to ensure the SC is a hard gate.

T008 and T044 are marked [X] (Complete) in the task list, yet the 'Rejected Tasks' section in the Analyze Report explicitly states that the error-handling framework and main orchestration logic are missing. Marking these as complete while the code is absent is a semantic weakening of the 'Complete' status, creating a false sense of progress. Furthermore, T057 (Phase 7) enforces CPU-only inference, but T008/T044 (marked complete) are the entry points that should already enforce this. The status of T008/T044 must be corrected to [ ] (Pending) to reflect the actual implementation state, or the tasks must be redefined to match the missing code.

SC-002 requires comparing ASR against the baseline from the 'original MedMisBench paper'. T045-ExtractBaseline extracts the value, but neither it nor T045 explicitly mandates running the Reference-Validator Agent (Constitution Principle II) to verify the citation before extraction. This silently relaxes Constitution Principle II: the baseline value could be extracted from an unverified or mismatched source, violating the 'Verified Accuracy' constraint. A task step must be added to invoke the Reference-Validator Agent on the baseline citation before T045 proceeds.
